memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your offering while I meet with him over there." The LORD met with Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and give him this word." So he went to him and found him standing beside his offering, with the Moabite officials. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?" - Num 23:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again Balaam withdraws to meet with the Lord, and once again God puts His word in the prophet's mouth. The pattern repeats exactly. New location, same God, same sovereign control over the message. Balak eagerly asks, "What did the Lord say?" still hoping for a different answer.

There is something instructive in this repetition. God does not change His word to accommodate a second attempt. The same Lord who blessed Israel from the first height blesses them from the second. His purpose is steady, unmoved by Balak's fresh efforts to secure a curse.

This reveals the constancy of God. He is not fickle, not swayed by persistence or ceremony or changed circumstances. What He has determined, He will accomplish. Human beings may waver and shift, but God remains the same. His faithfulness does not bend to our attempts to manipulate Him.

For God's people, this unchanging nature is our security. The Lord who has blessed us in Christ does not reverse Himself. He is the same yesterday, today, and forever (Heb 13:8). When everything around us shifts, we can anchor our hope in a God who never changes. His word to us stands firm across every circumstance.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does God's unchanging nature give you security?
2. Do you trust that God will not reverse His word to His people?
3. What comfort do you find in a God who is the same forever?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Unchanging God, thank You that You do not waver or shift like we do. Anchor my hope in Your steady faithfulness, for You are the same yesterday, today, and forever. Amen.
